item.title: Hierarchical self-organization of framboidal pyrite enables biosignature preservation
item.dc:creator: Jing Gao
Wanghua Wu
Dongmei Wang
Yue Wang
item.description: Microscopic and spectroscopic observations of framboidal pyrite from the Gakkel Ridge support a 3-stage growth model, which is compatible with, but does not require, biological activity and can explain the preservation of biosignatures in framboidal structures Framboidal pyrite serves as a critical archive of mineralization and paleoenvironmental history, yet its formation remains contested between biological templating and abiotic self-organization. Integrating geometric and crystallographic analyses of framboidal pyrite from the Gakkel Ridge, we reveal a hierarchical architecture defined by fractal geometry (fractal dimensions of 1.7–1.9) and systematic core-to-rim gradients in crystallinity and lattice strain. These findings underpin a unified three-stage growth model: initiation by synchronous nucleation, advancement via diffusion-limited aggregation into a fractal skeleton, and finalization through surface-energy minimization driving spheroidization. This mechanism provides a universal abiotic explanation for framboidal formation across diverse mineral systems. While biological activity may provide the initial supersaturation pulse, the characteristic texture remains a robust outcome of physical forces. The resulting architecture optimizes biosignature preservation, wherein defect-rich cores adsorb organic matter encapsulated by high-crystallinity rims. These findings resolve the long-standing biotic-abiotic dichotomy, establishing framboids as physically inevitable products and robust geochemical proxies for decoding mineralogical biosignatures in both terrestrial and extraterrestrial contexts. item.description: Abstract Earthquakes disrupt terrestrial ecosystem carbon storage by triggering landslides and altering land cover, yet a global quantification of these carbon losses has been lacking. Here we quantify the global earthquake-induced carbon losses by combining vegetation models, land cover, carbon density, and earthquake records. Focusing on strong earthquakes worldwide between 2006 and 2018, we find that these events cause a cumulative loss of 38.86 ± 6.23 teragrams of carbon by 2022. Forest ecosystems require at least six years to begin recovery. These carbon losses are unevenly distributed across countries, with 84.6% of affected countries being emerging and developing economies. In Nepal and Ecuador, cumulative earthquake-induced carbon losses exceed half of their cumulative land-use change emissions during the post-earthquake period. Our study establishes a global benchmark for carbon losses from geophysical disturbances, offering a crucial reference for national carbon accounting and disaster resilience strategies. item.title: Distinct constraints but shared dynamics shape the macroevolution of volatile organic compound chemodiversity
item.dc:creator: Ziyue Xu
Jiadong Zhu
Xu Liu
Longjun Wu
item.description: Organisms produce volatile organic compounds for communication, defense and environmental responses, but how this chemodiversity evolved is unclear. This study shows that in gymnosperms, chemodiversity shows weak covariation, core compounds are highly integrated, and both evolve in a punctuated mode. Complex metabolic systems have evolved across the tree of life, producing remarkable chemodiversity, yet the structure and evolutionary modes underlying this diversity remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the macroevolution of chemodiversity using a comprehensive dataset of gymnosperm foliage volatile organic compounds (VOCs) collected from the literature. We find that chemodiversity is dominated by a small fraction of “core” compounds. Although few in number, these core VOCs are widespread and abundant. To understand the full picture, we investigate the macroevolution of both high-dimensional global chemodiversity, and the dominant core chemodiversity. We find that both global and core chemodiversity have evolved through similar dynamics: punctuated evolution rather than gradual drift. We also identify a dichotomy in constraint, where global chemodiversity exhibits weak covariance—reflecting high evolutionary lability—and the core chemodiversity is characterized by high covariance and strong integration. We perform ancestral state reconstruction and find that this complex system is not a recent innovation; the major, core VOCs were already established in ancestral lineages prior to the Carboniferous period. These findings not only reveal the hierarchical structure of the gymnosperm VOC system, with its underlying constraints and dynamics, but also provide a framework for exploring the structure and evolutionary dynamics of chemodiversity. item.title: Paleogeographic controls on Phanerozoic weathering rates and implications for climate regulation
item.dc:creator: R. J. Graham
B. B. Cael
M. Fu
D. S. Abbot
item.description: Abstract Earth’s climate has remained habitable for billions of years, a stability usually attributed to a negative feedback from silicate weathering – the chemical breakdown of silicate rocks on land, which consumes atmospheric carbon dioxide faster as climate warms. However, whether temperature or hydrology primarily drives this feedback remains uncertain. Here we show the two controls leave geographic fingerprints: in an ensemble of climate simulations with randomized continents, temperature-controlled weathering depends on tropical land fraction, whereas hydrology-controlled weathering depends on continental fragmentation. Stronger weathering removes more carbon dioxide, cooling the planet, so each regime predicts anti-correlation between temperature and its controlling geography. Reconstructed global temperatures spanning 480 million years are anti-correlated with tropical land fraction, except from roughly 295 to 200 million years ago – overlapping the supercontinent Pangea – when they anti-correlate with continental fragmentation. The mechanism stabilizing Earth’s climate may thus have evolved, with temperature control apparently dominant for most of this period. item.dc:creator: Sezim E. Güvercin
Sylvain Barbot

Mehmet Köküm
Zekang Yang

item.description: Crustal faults across geological settings are often enriched in phyllosilicates because of the hydrothermal alteration of wall rocks. The frictional behavior of these altered rocks at mid-crustal conditions remains poorly understood. Here, we show that mica-schist gouge under crustal hydrothermal conditions can host mixed behavior promoting shallow aseismic creep and confined seismic ruptures. We conduct triaxial deformation experiments on natural samples from the East Anatolian Fault, Turkey, and simulate the resulting dynamics on the Pütürge segment during seismic cycles using a physical model of rock friction and a realistic thermal structure. Mica schist exhibits potentially unstable weakening between 300° and 400°C, promoting depth-confined earthquakes. The frictional properties of mica schist are compatible with the 2020 moment magnitude ( M w ) 6.8 Elazığ earthquake and the northern rupture arrest of the 2023 M w 7.8 Kahramanmaraş event, illustrating how the thermal and lithological structure affects rupture style and segmentation. item.description: Recent paleomagnetic studies of Apollo and Chang’e returned samples suggest that the lunar dynamo was active from ∼4.2 billion years ago (Ga) and ceased by ∼1.0 Ga. However, uncertainties remain regarding the temporal and spatial distribution of the lunar paleomagnetic field, as almost all of the returned samples are from the nearside, except for those returned by Chang’e-6. Here, we present the first paleomagnetic analysis of a lunar meteorite, Northwest Africa 15528, which is a feldspathic regolith breccia likely from the farside of the Moon. Our results not only indicate that it recorded a near-zero magnetic field (below a few hundred nanoteslas) at ∼0.7 Ga but also show that lunar meteorites can provide critical paleomagnetic information. Combined with two young Apollo samples from the nearside, Apollo 15015 (formed at ∼0.9 Ga) and Apollo 15465 (formed at ∼0.5 Ga), our findings suggest the absence of a global dynamo-generated lunar magnetic field for the past one billion years. item.title: Topographic stress controls fissure segmentation and eruptive cone formation during the Laki and Eldgjá eruptions
item.dc:creator: Maria Hurley
Francesco Maccaferri
Thomas R. Walter
item.description: Abstract Elongated dykes in tectonic rifts feed extensive basaltic fissure eruptions, yet surface eruption sites are highly discontinuous and unpredictable. Here we show that along-strike topographic variations, and the associated stress gradients, correlate with this localisation. We investigate eruptive cones at the two most productive historical basaltic eruptions in Iceland, Laki (1783–1784) and Eldgjá (~939–940). Morphological analyses of > 300 cones reveal volume variations (10 0 –10 7 m 3 ) and segmentation along ~ 100 km of fissures. Comparing cone distribution and volumes along the rift zone with pre-eruptive stress models, we demonstrate that high topographic stress gradients inhibit cone growth. We identify a critical stress gradient threshold predicting where larger cones are inhibited, while horizontal stress gradient peaks predict the location of fissure gaps. Our findings establish an empirical and physical link between topographic stress and volcanic morphologies, complementing previous models with a quantitative framework that aims at improving the forecasting of along-rift vent locations and development. item.dc:creator: Suraj Bhatt

item.description: Friability of meteorites, the tendency to crumble under repeated low stresses, influences the collisional and geological evolution of asteroids and small planetary bodies. Here, we quantify meteorite friability through laboratory tumbling experiments on a broad range of stony near-Earth objects. Disaggregation follows a bounded multiplicative process: it first accelerates with cumulative impacts, then slows as breakable material is exhausted. A log-logistic model describes this behavior and captures a material-dependent limit due to the “pillow-effect,” where accumulating fine debris cushions further impacts. The number of rotations needed for complete disaggregation varies by more than six orders of magnitude, indicating much broader timescales for regolith maturation and rubble-pile evolution than previously assumed. Fine dust generated from friable materials may also enhance cohesion under microgravity, helping explain the weak yet cohesive surfaces of rubble-pile asteroids such as Bennu and Ryugu. These measurements provide a framework for quantitatively incorporating friability into asteroid evolution models. item.title: Significant variability in marine hydrate stability
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kumar

item.description: “Bottom simulating reflections (BSR) vary over 100 s of meters and do not coincide with the calculated thermodynamic base of methane hydrate stability, as shown using 70 BSR measurements across the northern Gulf of Mexico.” Natural gas hydrate stores hundreds to thousands of gigatons of metastable carbon on Earth in a solid, ice-like clathrate. Hydrate stability is well defined in laboratory measurements, but we argue that fundamental constraints on hydrate stability are not understood in natural systems. In marine seismic data, bottom simulating reflections (BSR) are thought to mark the base of the hydrate stability zone. BSRs usually parallel the seafloor and deepen in the sediment column as water depths increase. Herein, we observe that BSR depths from 70 BSRs across the northern Gulf of Mexico vary over 100 s of meters and do not coincide with the calculated thermodynamic base of methane hydrate stability. BSR depths also do not have a strong correlation with water depth. Moreover, at several locations in deepwater, BSRs approach the seafloor suggesting hydrate here could be at risk of dissociation. Subsurface salt appears to control broad trends in BSR depths in the Gulf of Mexico, but there are still unaccounted processes influencing the stability of hydrate systems. item.description: Groundwater depletion undermines water security and contributes to atmospheric carbon dioxide emissions through dissolved carbon release and energy use for groundwater pumping. item.description: A redox disparity between Archean modified and ambient mantle, analogous to that between modern arc and mid-ocean ridge (MOR) mantle, hints at the operation of subduction on the early Earth; however, the geochemical agents responsible for Archean mantle oxidation remain ambiguous. Here we assess the redox capacity of volatiles released from Archean hydrothermally altered oceanic crust (AOC) using combined geodynamic and thermodynamic modeling. We show that the slab-top thermal structure governs the depth and extent of AOC dehydration, whereas the bulk-rock ferric-to-total iron ratio (XFe3+) modulates the speciation and concentration of carbon and sulfur in coexisting aqueous fluids. Reduced AOC predominantly mobilizes carbon and sulfur during late-stage dehydration, while oxidized AOC promotes earlier sulfur release and generates sulfate-rich fluids. item.description: Abstract Porphyry deposits represent globally significant sources of Cu and Mo, yet the magmatic volatile controls on Cu versus Mo metallogenic divergence remain poorly quantified in collisional settings. Here, we compare porphyry Cu systems from the Gangdese belt, southern Tibet, with porphyry Mo systems from the southern margin of the North China craton—two collisional belts with contrasting magma sources and metal endowments. By integrating apatite geochemistry with thermodynamic forward modeling, we reconstructed volatile evolution during ore-forming magma differentiation. Copper-forming magmas were more hydrous (initial H2O contents of ~5–6 wt %) than Mo-forming magmas (~3.8–4.7 wt %), whereas both were moderately oxidized. Modeled fluid-saturation thresholds are ~11 wt % H2O for Cu systems (~0.5 GPa) and ~9.2 wt % H2O for Mo systems (~0.4 GPa). Copper-related magmas were initially enriched in Cl (0.25–0.35 wt %) and F (0.40–0.55 wt %) but underwent significant F depletion (bulk DFc/m≈1.8) driven by early, extensive amphibole fractionation. In contrast, Mo-related magmas had lower initial F (0.05–0.25 wt %) and comparable Cl (0.20–0.35 wt %) but became progressively enriched in both halogens DFc/m≈0.7; DClc/m≈0.14 during prolonged crystallization with limited amphibole crystallization. item.description: Abstract The mobility of aqueous fluids in subducting slabs fundamentally controls volatile and element cycling, yet the efficiency of fluid extraction from eclogitized oceanic crust remains poorly constrained. The addition of NaCl reduces garnet–fluid–garnet, garnet–fluid–clinopyroxene, and clinopyroxene–fluid–clinopyroxene θ below the 60° interconnectivity threshold under all investigated conditions. Notably, fluid connectivity ( θ θ ≈ 0°) occurs at pressures ≥9 GPa and 1200°C. These results demonstrate that saline fluids form interconnected networks within eclogitized slabs, enabling efficient and pervasive fluid release in global subduction zones. This mechanism provides a direct mechanism for continuous element fluxing, metasomatism, and flux melting in the mantle wedge. Consequently, our findings imply that subducting oceanic crust is unlikely to transport significant free water to the deep mantle; instead, the deep mantle water inventory may be governed by water stored in hydrous and/or nominally anhydrous minerals. item.description: The Jinchanggou gold deposit (JGD) is a typical quartz vein-type deposit found in the Maoling ore field, which is mainly composed of altered-rock-type gold deposits. Time-resolved elemental depth profiles lack any obvious Au peaks and all data points are below the gold solid-solubility line on the Au/As diagram, implying that gold exists as lattice-bound Au+ in pyrite. A progressive increase in pyrite Co/Ni ratios is observed from Stage I to Stage IV, whereas Py3 displays highly variable Co/Ni ratios (0.006–5.52), reflecting vigorous water–rock reaction between the ore-forming fluid and wall rock. item.description: Charnockitic magmatism records fundamental processes of crustal growth and stabilization in Archean cratons. Combined whole-rock Sm-Nd and zircon Lu-Hf data reveal a marked isotopic dichotomy: the Rio Seco charnockite exhibits predominantly juvenile signatures (ε Nd(t) up to + 0.6; ε Hf(t) up to + 2.0) derived from a depleted-mantle source, whereas the Pium norite and Café enderbite display evolved signatures (ε Nd(t) = –2.8 to –1.0; ε Hf(t) = –4.8 to –1.0) reflecting enriched-mantle sources with longer crustal residence times. item.description: The dynamic mechanisms driving north–south trending rifts in southern Tibet remain contentious. Sn and Cu were likely sourced from Sn-rich metasedimentary rocks and Cu-rich juvenile components. item.description: Duolong district, as one of the largest porphyry Cu-Au clusters in China, has magnetite wide spreading in porphyry intrusions and several porphyry deposits. In contrast, hydrothermal magnetite characterized by higher Cu, Pb, Co and Ni/Cr ratios (>1). Ni/Cr ratios and Ti and V contents indicate that magmatic magnetite crystallizes at a higher-temperature of ∼620-800 °C and near-FMQ redox conditions compare to that of hydrothermal magnetite formed at temperatures of ∼400-620 °C under more oxidizing conditions approaching the HM buffer. Hydrothermal magnetite shows a dispersed elemental distribution, like large variation of Ti, Vand Sn suggesting complex formation hydrothermal environments. Early low-grade Cu stage magnetite (Mag 2–1), which is mainly associated with quartz and pyrite, has higher Ti and V contents, compared to later main Cu mineralization stage magnetite (Mag 2–2), which is associated with chalcopyrite, bornite, quartz, and pyrite, suggesting a cooling process. This is coupled with sharply increasing Cu (±Mo, La, and locally Co) from Mag 2–1 to Mag 2–2, indicating precipitation of these metals may partly go into magnetite. Hydrothermal magnetite in the three deposits show difference that Ti, Al, Mn, Zn, and Ni are higher in the Duobuza and Naruo deposits, whereas Pb are higher in the Bolong deposit. These are consistent with different hydrothermal alteration features in these deposits that Duobuza and Naruo have wider area of higher-temperature potassic alteration, whereas Bolong has larger area of lower-temperature sericitic alteration. It suggests these elements are controlled by temperature, or alternatively, by a combination of temperature, pH, and hydrothermal fluid composition. Based on these findings, a four-quadrant magnetite discrimination scheme (Priority I-IV) is established to effectively distinguishes high-grade stage hydrothermal magnetite. Results suggest that low Ti + V contents and high Mo and Cu contents is a signature of high-grade mineralization center, thus can be used to guide exploration prospecting. item.description: The crust–mantle interactions and geodynamic regimes of late Archean continental crust formation and evolution are a hot topic in global Precambrian research. The Yudongzi Complex is a typical Archean basement unit in the northwestern Yangtze Craton and features Neoarchean tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG) gneisses, K-rich granitoids and metavolcanic rocks. (1) The ca. 2.67–2.64 Ga diorites, quartz diorites and granodiorites feature high Mg# (47–60) values, Sr + Ba (average 1480 ppm) contents and K2O/Na2O (0.36–1.06) ratios, which are typical of Archean sanukitoids. They have high zircon δ18O (5.61 ‰ to 7.26 ‰) values and positive zircon εHf(t) (+1.6 to +7.4) and whole-rock εNd(t) (+0.2 and +3.4) values and were formed by the partial melting of lithospheric mantle metasomatized by subduction-related fluids and sediment and oceanic slab melts. (2) The ca. 2.68 Ga TTGs are characterized by high Mg# (48–54) values and high Cr (9.19–29.07 ppm) and Ni (6.81–18.57 ppm) contents and are most likely derived from the partial melting of oceanic slabs contaminated by 1–10 % mantle peridotite. The ca. 2.51 Ga TTGs have lower Mg# values and MgO contents and are derived from the partial melting of juvenile mafic lower crust. (3) The ca. 2.50 Ga monzogranites display geochemical affinities to S-type granites and were generated by partial melting of ancient psammites. (4) The ca. 2.53 G a mafic rocks can be subdivided into arc-type rocks and N-MORB-type rocks on the basis of their geochemical characteristics. The N-MORB-type rocks were formed by interactions between asthenospheric-derived melts and the overlying metasomatized lithospheric mantle. The partial melting P–T conditions of the studied ca. 2.68 Ga and ca. 2.51 Ga slab-derived TTG magmas are estimated to have involved high pressures and temperatures. item.description: Archean cratons represent the oldest preserved cores of continental crust, assembled through over two billion years of magmatism and crustal reworking. item.description: Despite the economic significance of gold skarn deposits, the processes driving ore-forming fluid evolution, particularly the role of discrete magmatic fluid pulses, remain enigmatic. Garnet U-Pb ages constrain the gold skarn formation to ca. 108–105 Ma, broadly linking gold mineralization to the Early Cretaceous diorite stocks rather than the previously proposed late Permian granodiorite. The compositions of Grt1–Grt5 record a stepwise evolution from Adr96–99Grs0–2 through Adr46–76Grs22–51 and Adr25–43Grs55–72 to Adr0–14Grs86–100, then to Adr22–32Grs66–73. Microthermometric data indicate a trapping temperature of > 556 °C for Grt1, whereas Grt2–Grt5 record alternating temperature-pressure variations (491–640 °C, 360–1006 bar). item.description: Lunar volcanic glass beads preserve records of sulfur evolution in primitive lunar magmas and provide important constraints on the sulfur inventory of the lunar interior. Reconstruction of their pre-eruptive sulfur contents requires sulfur diffusivity data for lunar melts, which have remained largely unavailable. Here we experimentally determined sulfur diffusivities in three synthetic lunar basaltic melts, spanning compositions from Apollo green (low TiO2, 0.52 wt%) and orange (intermediate TiO2, 8.58 wt%) to red (high TiO2, 13.93 wt%), with SiO2 decreasing from 45.35 to 35.92 wt% and MgO from 16.00 to 11.00 wt%, using diffusion-couple experiments at 0.5 GPa and 1674–1876 K in a piston cylinder apparatus. Sulfur diffusivity increases systematically from green to orange to red glass compositions, with NBO/T rising from 1.76 to 2.49 to 2.82, respectively. At 1673 K, sulfur diffusivity in lunar melts is 6–13 times higher than that in terrestrial basaltic melts (NBO/T = 0.61–0.79), primarily owing to the more depolymerized structure of lunar melts. Combining these results with published experimental data, we develop a general parameterization for sulfur diffusivity in anhydrous lunar and terrestrial silicate melts under reduced conditions as a function of temperature (T) and melt composition (X Si+Al, expressed by the combined mole fraction of Si + Al), which reproduces nearly all available experimental data within a factor of 2. Applying our new sulfur diffusivity data to Apollo green and orange glass beads yields revised pre-eruptive sulfur concentrations of 282–311 and 331 μg/g, corresponding to mantle source sulfur abundances of 9–28 and 27–63 μg/g, respectively. These estimates differ substantially from values previous inferred for Apollo and Chang’e mare basalts, indicating significant sulfur heterogeneity within the lunar interior, likely inherited from lunar magma ocean differentiation and subsequent mantle overturn. item.description: Sphalerite, a common sulfide in hydrothermal deposits, is one of the most significant hosts for critical metals such as Ga, Ge, In, and Se; however, distribution of these elements within sphalerites in volcanogenic massive sulfide (VMS) systems, along with geologic controls on their formation, remain inadequately understood. Sph-E1 and -E2 in No·I zone are marked by elevated Fe (up to 14.9 wt%) and Se (up to 1431 ppm) contents, with Se occurring as solid solution or galena micro-inclusions. Notably, Sph-E2 is further distinguished by its higher In (up to 158 ppm), Ag, Sb, and Sn contents, with trace element incorporation governed by substitution mechanisms of Ag+ + Sn2+ + In3+ ↔ 3Zn2+ and Ag+ + Sb3+ ↔ 2Zn2+. In contrast, sphalerites from No. III zone (Sph-W1 to W3) show relatively low Fe (average 5.4 wt%) and Se (average 66 ppm) concentrations. Integrated sphalerite chemistry, textural relationships with chalcopyrite, and GGIMFis geothermometry indicate that the high-Se Sph-E1 and Sph-E2 formed from high-temperature (282–329 °C), Se-rich hydrothermal fluids contributed by magmatic volatiles or fluids. All sphalerite from Xiaorequanzi exhibit low Ga, Ge, and In features, likely resulting from depletion of these elements in the source reservoir. These findings will enhance our understanding of critical metal distribution and enrichment in sphalerite for VMS and other hydrothermal systems.
